problems: The body is two separate round pucks with a visible seam where they overlap. It reads as a figure-8, not a guitar body with a smooth waist. Rebuild it as one outline: a warped cylinder with lower bout, waist and upper bout.
The fretboard runs over the sound hole, so the hole shows only as a half-covered black disc. On a real guitar the fretboard stops just before the hole's rosette.
The red pick guard overlaps the sound hole. It should sit beside the hole on the treble side, clear of the rosette.
The sound hole sits off-center on the upper puck. It should sit in the upper bout, just below where the neck joins the body.

The guitar lies almost level across a portrait card, so it fills about 80% of the width but only about a third of the height. The card asks for a large object, and wide plank bands are left empty above and below it. Turn it more steeply along the card's diagonal.

The top plate renders pale yellow, nearly the same color as the light planks, so the guitar does not stand out from the floor. The brief asks for warm wood brown: deepen the top, sides and neck, and make the porch planks a duller, darker weathered wood so they contrast.
The pick guard is a plain round disc that sits apart below the sound hole and reads as a red dot. Make it the usual teardrop shape tucked against the sound hole on the treble side.
